column1: # Canonical tier-1 prebuilt target table for fig-sys payload crates.
# Consumed by scripts/gen-payloads.sh, scripts/build-payload-lib.sh, and mirrored
# (by hand) into fig-sys/Cargo.toml cfg deps, fig-sys/build.rs payload_env_key,
# the workspace dependencies in Cargo.toml, and the publish list in
# .github/workflows/release.yml.
# Adding a target = one row here + rerun gen-payloads.sh + add the cfg dep,
# build.rs arm, workspace dependency and publish entry. Targets NOT listed here
# fall back to the vendored zig source build.
# Each payload carries the core (`libfig.a`, which has no language) and the
# library of every language fig ships (`libfig_<name>.a`), so neither fig-sys
# nor a language crate needs Zig on these targets.
# The macOS rows name their minimum OS for the same reason the iOS rows do,
# matching the defaults fig-sys's source build uses.
# The Android rows link no libc (Zig bundles no Bionic) and need no NDK.
# The wasm32-wasi row serves wasm32-wasip1 and wasm32-wasip2 alike: the
# library does no I/O.
# The iOS rows name their minimum OS (14.0, the lowest the arm64 simulator
# runs) because Zig otherwise stamps its own newer default into the archive.
# They also need Apple's iOS SDK, which Zig does not bundle, so the payloads
# are built on a macOS host.
# rust_target
aarch64-apple-darwin
x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
wasm32-unknown-unknown
aarch64-apple-ios
aarch64-apple-ios-sim
x86_64-apple-darwin
x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
aarch64-linux-android
x86_64-linux-android
wasm32-wasip1
